milestone.title: mp init AGENTS.md gaps — stale templates, missing cross-links, and unresolvable doc refs in consumer projects

intent.outcome: mp init produces correct, self-contained agent instructions that an agent can follow without missing doc references or stale paths, regardless of whether the project already has a root AGENTS.md.

problem.description: On consumer projects that adopt master-plan, the agent-instruction surface shipped by `mp init` is broken in four ways. (1) ROOT-AGENTS-SNIPPET.md uses project-relative `docs/...` references that don't resolve against the actual installed toolkit (~/.agents/master-plan/), so agents in consumer projects follow stale paths. (2) AGENTS-TEMPLATE.md does the same with `../docs/...` references — the project doesn't have a docs/ tree with mp content. (3) `mp init` silently skips when a root AGENTS.md already exists, so the user thinks init worked but the agent is missing critical instructions (or has stale ones). (4) There's no refresh path — once init has run, picking up template fixes requires manual surgery. The net effect: agents in consumer projects follow stale or unresolvable doc paths, leading to confused behavior or silent failures when they try to look up mp commands.

in_scope: Fix ROOT-AGENTS-SNIPPET.md doc references to match the installed toolkit layout
Decide what docs AGENTS-TEMPLATE.md should reference (toolkit-absolute paths vs project-relative) and fix them
Make mp init handle existing root AGENTS.md: warn, offer --force / --merge, or append the snippet
Add mp init --refresh to re-write master-plan/AGENTS.md from the current binary's template (or add a doctor check)
out_of_scope: Restructuring the installed toolkit docs tree (that's a separate documentation project)
Auto-updating root AGENTS.md on every mp command (too invasive)

acceptance_criteria.description: ROOT-AGENTS-SNIPPET.md references resolve correctly against the installed toolkit docs tree
acceptance_criteria.verification: grep -n 'docs/' templates/ROOT-AGENTS-SNIPPET.md; for each path: test -f ~/.agents/master-plan/<path>

acceptance_criteria.description: AGENTS-TEMPLATE.md doc references use toolkit-absolute paths (~/.agents/master-plan/docs/...) or a clear convention documented in the template so agents resolve them correctly
acceptance_criteria.verification: grep -rn '../docs/' templates/AGENTS-TEMPLATE.md returns no hits; every doc reference is resolvable from the installed toolkit at ~/.agents/master-plan/docs/

acceptance_criteria.description: mp init on a project with existing root AGENTS.md warns that the snippet was not inserted and tells the user what to add manually (or offers --force to overwrite / --merge to append)
mp init --refresh rewrites master-plan/AGENTS.md from the current binary's embedded template, with a dry-run or confirmation prompt

design_decisions.choice: Use toolkit-absolute paths (~/.agents/master-plan/docs/...) in templates, not project-relative ../docs/...
design_decisions.rationale: The installed toolkit is the canonical location for mp docs. Consumer projects don't have a docs/ directory with mp content. Toolkit-absolute paths survive regardless of where the project is checked out.

design_decisions.choice: Warn + print the snippet to stdout with instructions, offer --force flag to overwrite
design_decisions.rationale: Silently skipping is the worst behavior — the user thinks init worked but the agent is missing critical instructions. Overwriting without asking is destructive. Printing the snippet lets the user manually merge.

open_questions.question: Should we also vendor a minimal subset of toolkit docs into the project's master-plan/ so that doc references work even offline? Or rely entirely on the toolkit installation path?
open_questions.answer: Rely on toolkit-absolute paths (~/.agents/master-plan/docs/...) per the in-scope design decision. Vendoring a minimal subset into the project would duplicate content, drift from the canonical docs, and break the consumer-surface hygiene rule (templates/skills/** and templates/AGENTS-TEMPLATE.md must be self-contained without internal provenance). Trade-off accepted: offline use cases would need a separate mechanism — out of scope for M194; if needed, file as a follow-up (e.g., mp init --vendor-docs).

open_questions.question: For mp init --refresh: should it also refresh config.json / plan.json if the template defaults changed, or just AGENTS.md?
open_questions.answer: mp init --refresh rewrites master-plan/AGENTS.md only — scope is intentionally narrow and predictable. Config drift (config.json / plan.json schema changes) gets a separate doctor check (e.g., mp doctor config-drift) rather than being folded into a doc-refresh flag; folding config rewrites into --refresh is surprising and harder to revert. If schema-level config migration is needed, that's a separate mp config migrate command — out of scope for M194.

work_packages.name: Fix doc references in templates
work_packages.goal: Fix doc references in templates/ROOT-AGENTS-SNIPPET.md and templates/AGENTS-TEMPLATE.md to use toolkit-absolute paths (~/.agents/master-plan/docs/...) per the in-scope design decision. Resolves the 4-issue problem statement and unblocks consumer projects that currently have agents following stale or unresolvable doc paths.
work_packages.rollback: Revert the templates/ changes. Templates are pure files in the consumer-surface, so rollback is just a file revert.

work_packages.name: mp init handles existing root AGENTS.md
work_packages.goal: Make mp init's behavior explicit when a project already has a root AGENTS.md: print the snippet to stdout with instructions for manual merge, and accept --force (overwrite) and --merge (append). Eliminates the silent-skip behavior that leaves users thinking init worked.
work_packages.rollback: Revert the init mode changes. The default behavior returns to the previous silent-skip; the explicit modes are additive.

work_packages.name: mp init --refresh and tests
work_packages.goal: Add mp init --refresh to re-write master-plan/AGENTS.md from the current binary's embedded template, with a dry-run or confirmation prompt. Scope is AGENTS.md only (per Q-02). Test the suite_init integration tests (AC-03, AC-04) and verify the regression matrix (AC-01, AC-02).
work_packages.rollback: Revert the --refresh flag addition and the new test. Reverts to the pre-WP3 init command surface.

steps.action: Audit templates/ROOT-AGENTS-SNIPPET.md doc references; replace any project-relative paths (e.g. docs/...) with toolkit-absolute paths (~/.agents/master-plan/docs/...) per the design decision. Each replacement must resolve to an existing file at the toolkit install path.
steps.done_when: All doc references in ROOT-AGENTS-SNIPPET.md resolve to ~/.agents/master-plan/docs/... (per AC-01 verification).

steps.action: Audit templates/AGENTS-TEMPLATE.md doc references; replace any project-relative paths (e.g. ../docs/...) with toolkit-absolute paths (~/.agents/master-plan/docs/...). Every doc reference in the template must be resolvable from the installed toolkit location.
steps.done_when: No project-relative ../docs/ references remain in AGENTS-TEMPLATE.md; all references are toolkit-absolute.

steps.action: Modify mp init's existing-AGENTS.md path to print the snippet to stdout with manual-merge instructions; add --force (overwrite) and --merge (append) flags. The default behavior is the explicit warn + print; --force and --merge are opt-in.
steps.done_when: mp init on a project with an existing root AGENTS.md prints the snippet and the manual-merge instructions; --force overwrites; --merge appends.

steps.action: Add mp init --refresh that re-writes master-plan/AGENTS.md from the current binary's embedded template. Default: confirmation prompt; --yes to skip. Scope is AGENTS.md only (Q-02 resolution: config.json / plan.json drift is a separate doctor check, not folded into --refresh).
steps.done_when: mp init --refresh overwrites master-plan/AGENTS.md from the embedded template; --yes skips the prompt; config.json / plan.json are untouched.
